name: Accessory pairing sheet
plain: A system picker that pairs a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi accessory without a broad permission.
meaning: The app learns only about the accessory the person picks, which avoids scanning for everything nearby.

android.permission: Companion device association; no runtime permission for the chosen device
android.note: Chooser added in API 26; Android 16 adds device presence improvements

ios.note: Replaces broad Bluetooth and Local Network prompts for pairing; iOS 26 extends to more transports

limits.headline: Can pair a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi accessory you pick without scanning everything nearby
limits.user_action: You tap your accessory in the system pairing sheet
can: Show a system chooser with only matching accessories
Connect to the one accessory you choose
Replace the broad Bluetooth and local network prompts for pairing (iPhone)
cannot: Pick the accessory for you; you tap it
limits.differs: iPhone extends this to more connection types in iOS 26; Android uses a companion device chooser and added presence improvements in Android 16.

story.what_it_is: A system pairing sheet that connects a Bluetooth or Wi-Fi accessory without a broad permission.

marketing.name: AccessorySetupKit
marketing.pitch: Pair accessories using a simple system sheet. Apps see only the accessory you pick.

story.for_you: A tidy sheet shows your device with its picture and a Set up button. One tap and the gadget is ready. You are not asked to let the app scan everything nearby.
story.for_makers: The maker avoids a worrying permission prompt, so more buyers finish setup. The platform keeps the app away from neighbours' devices. It is a gentle push toward privacy by design.

use_cases.example: A watch or ring maker pairs with a phone app with one picture and one tap.
A smart plug or lamp finds your device without scanning for others in the building.
Earbuds appear in the sheet with the right colour and connect right away.
A tracker tag is set up in one tap and the app only sees that tag.
A baby monitor or thermometer pairs without exposing the family's other devices.
A camera or drone shows up on screen with its name and a pairing code.
A child's smartwatch pairs to a parent's phone for tracking without a permission wall.

risks: Only works for apps that adopt it
story.android_note: Android has a similar companion device pairing chooser, added in API 26, with presence improvements in Android 16.
story.ios_note: iOS 26 extends the pairing sheet to more kinds of links and replaces broad Bluetooth and local network prompts.

technical_bounds: App sees only the chosen accessory
